reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and the cited text supports it: the only licence grants in the quoted paragraphs run outbound from us (IBM) to the counterparty (MSL) — §13.3(a) confidential-information licence 'solely for IBM', §24.1(a) software access, and the Loaned Programs licence — so the restrictive, revocable and non-transferable characteristics benefit our side and are correctly not flagged.

§13.1/13.2 give us outright ownership plus assignment of MSL inventions on Products and on IBM processes, which is a stronger position than the preferred inbound licence (perpetual, irrevocable, affiliate/contractor scope); there is no grant to us that the counterparty could revoke at will.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline text was changed and no counterparty comment was raised — appropriate, since compliant findings are retained as internal evidence rather than negotiation issues.

The failed deterministic check on 'affiliates covered by the licence' is a heuristic mismatch here: with no inbound licence to us there is nothing to extend to affiliates, and the rationale properly records the absence of an IBM affiliate extension and of an MSL background-IP licence-back for transition as noted sub-elements rather than material deviations.
Successor/transfer mechanics are correctly deferred to §16.2/§16.5 under the assignment rule, avoiding double-flagging the same commercial term.
